name: Europe ↔ Asia Route via Suez
genZNote: This is the route that made the whole world realize how much global trade depends on one canal, back when a single stuck ship jammed it in 2021.

sections.heading: 🛳️ Route Path
bullets: European ports (Rotterdam, Hamburg, Marseille) → Mediterranean Sea → Suez Canal → Red Sea → Bab-el-Mandeb → Gulf of Aden/Arabian Sea → onward to India, Southeast Asia and East Asia via the Strait of Malacca.
The shortest sea route between Europe and Asia — the only alternative when it's disrupted is sailing all the way around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.

sections.heading: 📦 Why It Matters
bullets: Carries a very large share of world container trade and a meaningful share of world oil trade between Europe/the Middle East and Asia.
Passes through two chokepoints in sequence — the Suez Canal and Bab-el-Mandeb — making it sensitive to disruption at either point.
India's trade with Europe substantially uses this route, making both Suez and Bab-el-Mandeb strategically relevant to Indian trade even though neither lies within Indian waters.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Suez route is the shortest sea path between Europe and Asia, passing through the Mediterranean, Suez Canal, Red Sea and Bab-el-Mandeb.
keyFacts: Path: Europe → Mediterranean → Suez Canal → Red Sea → Bab-el-Mandeb → Indian Ocean → Asia.
Alternative when disrupted: around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
Passes through two chokepoints: Suez Canal and Bab-el-Mandeb.
commonConfusion: This route passes through TWO chokepoints, not one — don't name only the Suez Canal and forget Bab-el-Mandeb.

highYieldFacts: Suez route = shortest Europe-Asia sea path.
Chokepoints along it: Suez Canal, Bab-el-Mandeb.
Alternative route: Cape of Good Hope (around Africa).
commonTraps: The 2021 Ever Given grounding disrupted the Suez Canal specifically — a good example of a single-chokepoint failure affecting this whole route.
mustRemember: Suez route = Europe-Asia's shortest link; two chokepoints (Suez + Bab-el-Mandeb); Cape route is the fallback.
